candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Deuteronomy
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy, on 12:1-14. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On 'the place which the Lord your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there' (Deu 12:5), Ephrem reads the centralization-of-worship command as the canonical Old-Testament typological anchor that flows through Shiloh → Jerusalem → Zion → the Eucharistic altar of every local church. The Lord chooses ONE place for his Name in the Old Covenant; in the New Covenant, every Eucharistic altar is THE chosen place because the Body broken there IS the New-Covenant tabot. Tewahedo eucharistic theology cites Deu 12:5 as the canonical anchor for the doctrine that the Eucharist gathers Jerusalem's centralization into every parish — the tabot-bearing altar IS the chosen place.
